item.content:encoded:
ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-06-19

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 50 papers | Generated: 2026-06-19 02:44 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — June 19, 2026

Today's Highlights

Agent safety and robustness dominate today's submissions, with multiple papers addressing jailbreak resilience, policy adherence, and bias propagation in multi-agent settings. A cluster of work on KV-cache compression and efficient serving for context-heavy agents signals growing attention to deployment realities. On the architecture side, research probing LLM reasoning transparency (DiffusionGemma) and Lie-algebra attention mechanisms push theoretical foundations. Several papers also tackle calibration under distribution shift and continual learning forgetting dynamics, reflecting sustained interest in reliable, adaptable AI systems.

Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models

How Transparent is DiffusionGemma? http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20560v1 Engels, McDougall, Chughtai et al. Systematically analyzes reasoning transparency in DiffusionGemma, finding that continuous latent-space computation reduces interpretability compared to discrete-token models—critical for understanding model decisions and debugging.

What Do Safety-Aligned LLMs Learn From Mixed Compliance Demonstrations? http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20508v1 Dai, Patel Shows that mixing benign with harmful compliance demonstrations in-context can jailbreak safety-aligned LLMs, revealing how models interpret compliance signals ambiguously.

Calibration Without Comprehension: Diagnosing the Limits of Fine-Tuning LLMs for Vulnerability Detection in Systems Software http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20502v1 Zibaeirad, Vieira Introduces CWE-Trace, a 834-sample Linux kernel vulnerability benchmark across 74 CWEs, and finds that fine-tuned LLMs often pattern-match rather than genuinely reason about security.

The Token Is a Group Element: On Lie-Algebra Attention over Matrix Lie Groups http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20547v1 Musialski Proposes the first attention mechanism where tokens are bare matrix Lie group elements without feature payloads, offering a fundamentally new geometric perspective on transformer architectures.

Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20544v1 Wong, Prinster, Saria et al. Finds that enforcing calibration at individual expert levels improves ensemble accuracy and calibration under distribution shift, with practical implications for MoE deployment.

Multi-Task Bayesian In-Context Learning http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20538v1 Zhu, Oermann, Cho Formulates in-context learning as multi-task Bayesian inference, enabling principled uncertainty quantification without restrictive modeling assumptions.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning

LedgerAgent: Structured State for Policy-Adherent Tool-Calling Agents http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20529v1 Uddin, Saeidi, Blanco et al. Introduces structured state management for tool-calling agents in customer service, maintaining task states across turns while enforcing domain policies—addresses a key operational gap.

Beyond Global Replanning: Hierarchical Recovery for Cross-Device Agent Systems http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20487v1 Yao, Luo, Long et al. Proposes hierarchical recovery strategies for multi-device agents, moving beyond coarse-grained replanning to handle dynamic runtime failures across heterogeneous environments.

Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20493v1 Liu Formally models how evaluator biases spread through multi-agent LLM networks, demonstrating in controlled experiments that systematic biases propagate and amplify across agents.

LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20408v1 Lee, Choi, Kim et al. Presents NRT-Bench, a multi-turn red-teaming benchmark for LLM agents in safety-critical roles, revealing poor robustness under sustained adversarial pressure.

Sovereign Execution Brokers: Enforcing Certificate-Bound Authority in Agentic Control Planes http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20520v1 He, Yu Proposes certificate-bound authority enforcement for autonomous agents, ensuring production mutation authority is cryptographically separated from non-deterministic reasoning.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks

FlowEdit: Associative Memory for Lifelong Pronunciation Adaptation in Flow-Matching TTS http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20518v1 Singh, Singh, Mathur Introduces a lifelong adaptation framework for frozen flow-matching TTS that corrects pronunciation errors without retraining, using associative memory for out-of-vocabulary proper nouns.

UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20474v1 Chakrabarti, Limpus, Rana et al. Demonstrates 4-bit KV-cache compression for context-heavy agents using TurboQuant-style rotation and codebooks, addressing memory pressure from long-prefix reuse.

Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20475v1 Yang, Zheng, Cheng et al. Proposes cross-batch, operation-level evidence accumulation to distinguish stably effective agent operations from accidental hits in batch-style trace distillation.

DeepSWIP: Quotient-WMC Counterfactuals for Neural Probabilistic Logic Programs http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20526v1 Habib, Belle, He Introduces a single-world counterfactual semantics for DeepProbLog-style neurosymbolic systems, enabling causal reasoning beyond associational inference.

Fisher-Geometric Sharpness and the Implicit Bias of SGD toward Flat Minima http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20469v1 Ahmed, Sarmah, Dutta Develops a reparametrization-invariant measure of flatness using Fisher information geometry, providing theoretical grounding for why SGD finds flat minima that generalize better.

📊 Applications

StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20527v1 Kolli, Cavelius, Nikeghbal et al. Identifies that a small set of visual stylistic cues (e.g., lighting, framing) drives most social biases in multimodal LLMs, enabling targeted debiasing interventions.

Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20517v1 Ivanova, Zadorozhny, Levichev et al. Extends LiveCodeBench to multi-language code generation evaluation, providing contamination-aware benchmarks for Python, Java, C++, and Go.

SARLO-80: Worldwide Slant SAR Language Optic Dataset 80cm http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20523v1 Debuysère, Trouvé, Letheule et al. Releases a large-scale SAR-optical dataset with preserved slant-range geometry and 80cm resolution, enabling multimodal foundation model training for synthetic aperture radar.

Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology http://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20477v1 Salcan, Ging, Schirrmeister et al. Introduces RefRad2D, a 1.2M-pair bilingual radiology dataset, and shows how to train spatially grounded VLMs for medical imaging without manual annotations.

Research Trend Signal

A convergence of agent safety and formal verification approaches is visible today. Papers on probabilistic verification (Solko-Breslin et al.), certificate-bound authority (He & Yu), and defensive misdirection (Soosahabi & Namsani) indicate a shift from ad-hoc safety measures toward principled, verifiable agent control. Meanwhile, several works on "marginal advantage accumulation" and "memory-driven self-evolution" point to a growing interest in making agents learn stably from their own experience without catastrophic forgetting. The KV-cache work (UltraQuant) and execution-state checkpointing (Execution-State Capsules) suggest that agent deployment at scale is driving new infrastructure demands. Finally, the multiplicity of bias/fairness papers—covering visual cues, data mitigation, and contagion networks—reflects an active community effort to move bias measurement from static datasets to dynamic, multi-agent contexts.

Worth Deep Reading

  1. How Transparent is DiffusionGemma? (Engels et al.) — Essential for anyone building on DiffusionGemma or interested in reasoning transparency in non-autoregressive architectures. The empirical methodology for probing continuous latent-space reasoning is novel and broadly applicable.

  2. Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems (Liu) — A rigorous formal framework with controlled experiments that quantifies how biases amplify in agent networks. This has direct implications for any deployed multi-agent system.

  3. Fisher-Geometric Sharpness and the Implicit Bias of SGD toward Flat Minima (Ahmed et al.) — Provides a long-needed reparametrization-invariant measure of flatness, resolving theoretical tensions in the flat-minima literature. Relevant for understanding generalization in all deep learning systems.

item.content:encoded:
Hugging Face 热门模型日报 2026-06-19

数据来源: Hugging Face Hub | 共 30 个模型 | 生成时间: 2026-06-19 02:44 UTC

好的，作为AI模型生态分析师，这是为您生成的2026年6月19日《Hugging Face 热门模型日报》。

Hugging Face 热门模型日报 | 2026年6月19日

今日速览

本周 Hugging Face 生态呈现“巨无霸落地”与“百花齐放微调”的双重景象。DeepSeek-V4-Pro 以近5000点赞登顶，巩固了开源大模型的领先地位。同时，社区对 Gemma-4 和 Qwen3.6 系列的量化与微调热情高涨，涌现出大量 GGUF 和“无审查”变体，证明了前沿模型强大的生命力与社区适配能力。多模态模型依然是绝对主流，超过半数的热门模型具备图像理解能力，而来自 NVIDIA 的 LocateAnything-3B 则开辟了“感知-定位”这一细分赛道，显示出专业任务的巨大潜力。

热门模型

🧠 语言模型（LLM、对话模型、指令微调）

  • deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro 作者: deepseek-ai | 点赞: 4,957 | 下载: 2,948,726 一句话说明: 新版旗舰级语言模型，强大的对话与推理能力使其成为当前开源社区的绝对焦点，一骑绝尘的点赞数证明了其地位。

  • google/gemma-4-12B-it 作者: google | 点赞: 1,085 | 下载: 1,309,625 一句话说明: Google 的 Gemma-4 指令版本，定位为“任意模态处理”模型，其强大的基础能力催生了社区海量的微调与量化活动。

  • zai-org/GLM-5.2 作者: zai-org | 点赞: 1,350 | 下载: 4,307 一句话说明: 智谱 AI 的最新一代 GLM MoE 模型，以对话为核心任务，是国产大模型在开源社区的重要代表。

🎨 多模态与生成（图像、视频、音频、文本到X）

  • nvidia/LocateAnything-3B 作者: nvidia | 点赞: 2,165 | 下载: 183,093 一句话说明: NVIDIA 推出的“任何物体定位”模型，通过图像特征提取实现精准定位，开辟了多模态模型在“感知”层面的新应用场景。

  • HauhauCS/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive 作者: HauhauCS | 点赞: 1,971 | 下载: 3,420,052 一句话说明: 基于 Qwen3.6 的“激进派”无审查 MoE 变体，凭借极高的下载量和话题性反映了社区对模型“自由度”的巨大需求。

  • google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it 作者: google | 点赞: 1,002 | 下载: 527,080 一句话说明: Google 的 Diffusion 版 Gemma，将扩散模型架构与对话能力结合，是“生成式”模型领域的一次重要尝试和创新。

  • MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 作者: MiniMaxAI | 点赞: 1,102 | 下载: 56,162 一句话说明: MiniMax 的旗舰多模态模型，具备图像与文本理解能力，是国产多模态模型的有力竞争者。

🔧 专用模型（代码、数学、医疗、嵌入）

  • yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1-GGUF 作者: yuxinlu1 | 点赞: 1,712 | 下载: 211,424 一句话说明: 基于 Gemma-4 的代码专用模型，经过特定合成数据（Fable5, Composer2.5）微调并量化，是“小而强”代码模型的代表。

  • moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code 作者: moonshotai | 点赞: 887 | 下载: 229,156 一句话说明: 月之暗面（Kimi）推出的代码版模型，采用压缩张量技术，专注于代码生成与特征提取，下载量极高。

  • WeiboAI/VibeThinker-3B 作者: WeiboAI | 点赞: 410 | 下载: 6,589 一句话说明: 微博AI出品的3B小模型，主打数学推理能力，证明了小参数模型在垂直领域仍有出色表现。

📦 微调与量化（社区微调、GGUF、AWQ）

  • unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF 作者: unsloth | 点赞: 653 | 下载: 918,431 一句话说明: unsloth 对官方 Gemma-4 的 GGUF 量化版，极大降低了部署门槛，是社区用户使用该模型的首选入口。

  • DavidAU/Qwen3.6-40B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Deckard-Heretic-Uncensored-Thinking-NEO-CODE-Di-IMatrix-MAX-GGUF 作者: DavidAU | 点赞: 394 | 下载: 529,069 一句话说明: 典型的社区“缝合怪”模型，集成了Qwen、Claude等多种特性进行无审查微调，反映了社区对极致性能与自由度的追求。

  • OBLITERATUS/Gemma-4-12B-OBLITERATED 作者: OBLITERATUS | 点赞: 350 | 下载: 96,805 一句话说明: 另一个知名的“无审查”Gemma-4 微调版本，延续了社区对“破除限制”的持续探索。

生态信号

本周生态信号强劲，主要有三点：第一，DeepSeek-V4-Pro 和 Gemma-4 家族构成了本周生态的两大核心，前者代表“最强性能”，后者代表“最强社区活跃度”。第二，开源模型在与闭源模型的竞争中表现出强大的生命力，不仅性能持续追赶，更通过社区微调提供了大量闭源模型无法提供的定制化版本（如各种无审查、编码增强等）。第三，量化活动（尤其是 GGUF 格式）依然是社区最重要的“基建”环节，几乎所有热门模型都第一时间被 unsloth 等团队量化，这说明部署效率和可用性依然是社区关注的第一优先级。

值得探索

  1. nvidia/LocateAnything-3B：它跳出了常规的对话或生成范式，专注于“感知-定位”这一细分任务。对于从事机器人、自动驾驶或图像编辑的开发者和研究者来说，这个模型提供了一种新颖且强大的工具，值得深入探索其原理与使用边界。

  2. google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it：结合了扩散模型和大型语言模型的创新架构值得高度关注。虽然其任务被列为 image-text-to-text，但其背后的“扩散生成”理念可能与传统的自回归模型有本质不同，这可能是通往下一代生成式AI的钥匙。

  3. WeiboAI/VibeThinker-3B：在追求大模型极致性能的浪潮中，一个仅有3B参数的模型，却在数学推理任务上获得如此关注，非常值得研究。这表明通过特定的架构设计或训练数据，小模型在特定、高逻辑性任务上可以达到惊人的效果，对于资源受限但需要高精度推理的场景极具价值。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

Hugging Face Trending Models Digest 2026-06-19

Source: Hugging Face Hub | 30 models | Generated: 2026-06-19 02:44 UTC

Here is the structured Hugging Face Trending Models Digest for 2026-06-19.

1. Today's Highlights

The open-weight model ecosystem is experiencing a major inflection point, driven by a surge in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures and aggressive community quantization. DeepSeek’s DeepSeek-V4-Pro dominates the charts with nearly 5,000 weekly likes, signaling strong demand for frontier-level conversational models. The landscape is also defined by a wave of uncensored, role-play, and "heretic" fine-tunes based on Qwen 3.6, alongside new first-party MoE releases like Google’s DiffusionGemma and zai-org’s GLM-5.2. Multimodal models are no longer niche—most top entries now support vision, and even code models come paired with image-text-to-text pipelines.

2. Trending Models

🧠 Language Models (LLMs, chat models, instruction-tuned)

  • deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
    Author: deepseek-ai | Likes: 4,957 | Downloads: 2,948,726
    The week's most-liked model; a frontier MoE conversational model driving community excitement around open-weight LLM performance.

  • zai-org/GLM-5.2
    Author: zai-org | Likes: 1,350 | Downloads: 4,307
    A new MoE conversational model from zai-org, likely a successor to GLM series, gaining traction for efficiency and dialogue quality.

  • yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1-GGUF
    Author: yuxinlu1 | Likes: 1,712 | Downloads: 211,424
    A specialized coding variant of Gemma-4-12B, popular for reasoning and code generation in a quantized GGUF format.

  • microsoft/FastContext-1.0-4B-SFT
    Author: microsoft | Likes: 205 | Downloads: 957
    A small yet capable 4B instruction-tuned model optimized for long-context tasks via the "Explorer SubAgent" approach.

  • nex-agi/Nex-N2-Pro
    Author: nex-agi | Likes: 329 | Downloads: 6,640
    A Qwen3.5-based MoE model bridging text and vision, gaining attention for its balanced size-to-performance ratio.

  • lordx64/Qwable-v1
    Author: lordx64 | Likes: 120 | Downloads: 836
    A fine-tune on Qwen3.5 MoE, catering to users who want enhanced Qwen capabilities beyond vanilla releases.

🎨 Multimodal & Generation (image, video, audio, text-to-X)

  • google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it
    Author: google | Likes: 1,002 | Downloads: 527,080
    Google’s new DiffusionGemma family—a 26B MoE model for image-text-to-text, combining diffusion concepts with Gemma architecture.

  • MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3
    Author: MiniMaxAI | Likes: 1,102 | Downloads: 56,162
    A flagship multimodal agent model (image-text-to-text), trending for its MoE design and high-quality visual reasoning.

  • moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code
    Author: moonshotai | Likes: 887 | Downloads: 229,156
    A code-focused multimodal model from Moonshot AI (Kimi), integrating vision and code through compressed-tensors for efficiency.

  • nvidia/LocateAnything-3B
    Author: nvidia | Likes: 2,165 | Downloads: 183,093
    NVIDIA’s image-feature-extraction and localization model, surging in popularity for spatial understanding and object grounding tasks.

  • zai-org/SCAIL-2
    Author: zai-org | Likes: 228 | Downloads: 0
    A pose-driven video generation model (image-to-video), notable for character animation and diffusion-based video synthesis.

  • bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b
    Author: bosonai | Likes: 489 | Downloads: 57,380
    A 4B text-to-speech model from the Higgs audio family, trending for natural voice synthesis using multimodal Qwen backbones.

  • Zyphra/ZONOS2
    Author: Zyphra | Likes: 115 | Downloads: 669
    A new open-source TTS model under Apache 2.0, gaining attention for license openness and US-region focus.

  • owensong/Inflect-Nano-v1
    Author: owensong | Likes: 90 | Downloads: 0
    An ultra-small TTS model for edge or low-latency deployment, interesting for research on minimalistic speech synthesis.

🔧 Specialized Models (code, math, medical, embeddings)

  • WeiboAI/VibeThinker-3B
    Author: WeiboAI | Likes: 410 | Downloads: 6,589
    A Qwen2-based math-reasoning model, trending for its surprising strength in mathematical problem-solving at a 3B scale.

  • nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b
    Author: nvidia | Likes: 541 | Downloads: 13,033
    A streaming automatic speech recognition model (0.6B), using cache-aware architecture for low-latency voice applications.

  • CohereLabs/North-Mini-Code-1.0
    Author: CohereLabs | Likes: 449 | Downloads: 15,285
    A code-focused MoE model from Cohere (under the North series), combining conversational ability with code generation.

📦 Fine-tunes & Quantizations (community fine-tunes, GGUF, AWQ)

  • HauhauCS/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive
    Author: HauhauCS | Likes: 1,971 | Downloads: 3,420,052
    The most downloaded model this week—an uncensored, aggressive-tuned Qwen 3.6 MoE in GGUF, driving massive community experimentation.

  • DavidAU/Qwen3.6-40B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Deckard-Heretic-Uncensored-Thinking-NEO-CODE-Di-IMatrix-MAX-GGUF
    Author: DavidAU | Likes: 394 | Downloads: 529,069
    An extreme fine-tune merging Qwen 3.6 with "Claude-style" thinking & uncensored behavior, popular for role-play and creative use.

  • OBLITERATUS/Gemma-4-12B-OBLITERATED
    Author: OBLITERATUS | Likes: 350 | Downloads: 96,805
    A community "obliterated" (uncensored) variant of Gemma-4-12B, trending for jailbreak-style fine-tuning on top of Google’s official release.

  • unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF
    Author: unsloth | Likes: 653 | Downloads: 918,431
    Unsloth’s GGUF quantization of Google’s Gemma-4-12B-it, highly popular for enabling local inference on consumer hardware.

  • unsloth/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-GGUF
    Author: unsloth | Likes: 307 | Downloads: 164,209
    The quantized version of DiffusionGemma, making Google’s multimodal MoE accessible to local users.

3. Ecosystem Signal

The ecosystem is in the midst of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) renaissance. Models explicitly tagged as moe (Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE, GLM MoE, DiffusionGemma, Cohere MoE) dominate the top of the leaderboard. This reflects a structural shift: users and open-source practitioners are prioritizing high performance per parameter, making MoE the new default architecture.

On the open-weight vs. proprietary front, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Google’s Gemma/DiffusionGemma series are the week’s strongest open-weight signal, rivaling proprietary capabilities. The trend is clearly toward frontier openness, not just for base models but for specialized, uncensored, and role-play variants.

Quantization and fine-tuning remain the driving force of community engagement. Unsloth alone accounts for four entries on the list—all GGUF quantizations of major new models. Meanwhile, "uncensored" and "heretic" fine-tunes (Qwen 3.6 variants, Gemma-4-OBLITERATED) represent a parallel, fast-moving subculture that drives massive download volumes (up to 3.4M). This indicates a widening divide between safety-aligned corporate releases and a vocal user base that demands unrestricted models.

4. Worth Exploring

  1. nvidia/LocateAnything-3B – With 2,165 likes and a 3B scale, this model offers a rare combination of high-quality object localization with a lightweight footprint. It’s a strong candidate for real-world vision AI pipelines and edge deployment.

  2. google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it – As a first-of-its-kind diffusion+LLM hybrid from Google, this model represents a novel architectural direction. The 26B MoE design with image-text-to-text capability makes it a fascinating study model for researchers exploring multimodal generation.

  3. unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF – With 918k downloads, this is the definitive local-run version of Gemma-4. For anyone wanting to test Google’s latest architecture on a single GPU, this GGUF is the most practical entry point this week.

This digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.
